item.title: LBW releases fall honor lists
item.description: LBW Community College honored 244 students on its Fall 2025 President’s and Dean’s Lists, including several from Georgiana, Greenville and McKenzie.

item.title: The art of interviewing poorly
item.description: A humorously bad-interview guide morphs into real advice on handling nerves, preparation, and what to wear before a job interview you really want.

item.title: Growing roots for the community
item.description: Butler County Forestry Planning Committee’s Jan. 31 Tree Seedling Sale offers $2 trees and shrubs, supporting forestry workshops and a June youth camp.

item.title: Locals commended on UWA honors lists
item.description: Butler County students earn spots on UWA fall 2025 Dean's and President's Lists, recognized for GPAs above 3.25 with no grade below C.

item.title: Middle District of Alabama Recognizes National Human Trafficking Prevention Month
item.description: Middle District of Alabama marks National Human Trafficking Prevention Month, highlighting Homeland Security Task Forces, recent sex trafficking convictions and nationwide surge operations.

item.title: Joseph William Jones - Obituary
item.description: Joseph William Jones, Jr. (Billy) was born Feb. 13, 1945 in Monroeville to Joseph William Jones, Sr. and Jennie Lee Urquhart Jones. He passed away peacefully at his home on Jan. 23 surrounded by his family. Billy attended Murphy High School in Mobile and later Monroe County High School in Monroeville. item.title: Mobile market to return to Georgiana
item.description: UAB Mobile Market returns to Georgiana Jan. 30, giving residents renewed access to fresh food as the town’s permanent grocery stays closed for remodeling.

item.title: Butler County Arrests Jan. 12 - 25
item.description: Butler County releases Jan. 12–25 arrest log, detailing charges ranging from failure to appear and DUI to drug offenses, domestic violence and theft.

item.title: Lions Club meets Greenville High football coach
item.description: New Greenville High head football coach Gary Johnston shares his move from Foley and vision for the Tigers with the Greenville Lions Club.
